title: Northwest Flight 2501, 1950: the Airliner Lake Michigan Never Gave Back

sources.what: left LaGuardia at night on June 23, 1950; killing all 58 on board; debris washed ashore in South Haven; a 20-year search ended in 2025 without finding the wreckage
a DC-4 that disappeared over Lake Michigan with 58 aboard, en route to Seattle; went down in a thunderstorm
'the worst airline disaster in U.S. history' (at the time)
'the deadliest commercial airline crash in U.S. history' at the time; remains washed ashore in South Haven
a storm had developed over Lake Michigan
the 'Lake Michigan Triangle' and its mysterious events
the plane 'mysteriously disappeared in the waters off St. Joseph'

beats.text: 58 people were lost over Lake Michigan, and the plane has never been found.
beats.label: LAKE MICHIGAN, 1950

beats.text: On June 23, 1950, Northwest Flight 2501 took off from New York, bound for Seattle.
beats.label: JUNE 23, 1950

beats.text: Just after midnight, over Lake Michigan, it flew into a storm. Then it went silent.
beats.label: THE STORM

beats.text: All 58 people on board were lost. At the time, it was the deadliest commercial airline crash in American history.
beats.label: 58 LIVES

beats.text: Debris washed ashore near South Haven, Michigan.
beats.label: SOUTH HAVEN

beats.text: In 2025, the Michigan Shipwreck Research Association ended its 20-year search. It never found the wreck.
beats.label: NEVER FOUND

beats.text: Some call these waters the Lake Michigan Triangle.
beats.label: THE LEGEND

beats.text: Comment your town for the next La Porte After Dark.

end_card.pill: South Haven and St. Joseph, Michigan
